investigator.agent: the course agent loop agent.py (Lab 4 package)

hypotheses.hypothesis: The cause of checkout errors during 07:00Z–07:20Z on 2026-10-24 is **PaymentService/Charge failures**.
hypotheses.evidence: Payment's Charge server spans failed at 0.0073/s over the 5 minutes to 07:13, the window fully inside the fault; on the baseline at 07:03:06 payment had no error series at all, so the query is empty there. The failures are those of checkout's orders (same two calls in both services' counters).

hypotheses.hypothesis: This is evidenced by the consistent spike in `oteldemo.PaymentService/Charge` errors (2 errors per 5-second interval) starting at 07:17:20Z, directly coinciding with the checkout error surge observed in the same time window.
hypotheses.predicts: sum(increase(traces_span_metrics_calls_total{service_name="payment", span_kind="SPAN_KIND_SERVER", span_name="oteldemo.PaymentService/Charge", status_code="STATUS_CODE_ERROR"}[12m])) > 0 unless on() sum(increase(traces_span_metrics_calls_total{service_name="payment", span_kind="SPAN_KIND_SERVER", span_name="oteldemo.PaymentService/Charge", status_code="STATUS_CODE_ERROR"}[2m])) > 0
hypotheses.evidence: The component held: Charge errors rose in the 12 minutes to 07:19 (left side true), and none on the baseline. The time did not: there was no Charge error between 07:17 and 07:19 (right side empty), because paymentFailure was switched off at 07:11:41. The agent read the cumulative counter, which stays at 2 after the last failure, as '2 errors per 5-second interval' and placed the spike at 07:17:20, six minutes after the errors had ended.

hypotheses.hypothesis: **Hypothesis 1**: Payment processing timeouts caused by external payment gateway failures.
hypotheses.evidence: No timeouts: payment's p95 was 3.3 ms at 07:13 (3.9 ms on the baseline), so a p95 above one second returns nothing. The charges failed fast; there is no external gateway in the demo's payment service and nothing slowed down.

hypotheses.hypothesis: **Hypothesis 2**: Rate limiting or backend service overload in the payment processor triggered checkout failures.
hypotheses.evidence: No overload: payment served 0.095 requests/s at 07:13 against 0.092/s on the baseline, so more than twice the baseline returns nothing. The payment failures came with unchanged traffic; the load surge of the incident hit the frontend only.

hypotheses.hypothesis: This aligns with the span name `oteldemo.CheckoutService/PlaceOrder` (which likely depends on `PaymentService/Charge` to finalize transactions), explaining why checkout errors directly cascade from payment failures.
hypotheses.predicts: sum(rate(traces_span_metrics_calls_total{service_name="checkout", span_kind="SPAN_KIND_SERVER", status_code="STATUS_CODE_ERROR"}[5m])) / sum(rate(traces_span_metrics_calls_total{service_name="checkout", span_kind="SPAN_KIND_SERVER"}[5m])) > 0.05 and on() sum(rate(traces_span_metrics_calls_total{service_name="payment", span_kind="SPAN_KIND_SERVER", span_name="oteldemo.PaymentService/Charge", status_code="STATUS_CODE_ERROR"}[5m])) > 0
hypotheses.evidence: Both held together at 07:13: 7.4 % of checkout's requests failed and payment's Charge failed at 0.0073/s; on the baseline neither side returns anything. Checkout's error counter and payment's moved by the same two calls, so checkout's failures are payment's, passed on to the order.
